canonical_data: the open Unreal project and level itself, plus plugin settings in the editor's project configuration; chat history lives in the editor session
current_repo_note: The GitHub description ("A collection of Unreal Engine 5 Editor Utility widgets powered by GPT3/4") predates the current UnrealGPT plugin; the README, plugin descriptor and commits describe the plugin. The bundled Geist and Geist Mono font files ship without a licence file in the plugin.
strengths: Purpose-built editor tools go beyond a bare script runner: atomic actor tools with Undo, native Blueprint query, node, pin and compile tools, a scene query, viewport screenshots and an editor log reader
The instructions tell the agent to verify its own changes with scene queries and screenshots, and a clarify tool lets it stop and ask the user before acting on an ambiguous request
An MCP client over stdio and HTTP, a tool-iteration cap (100 by default) and a Python execution timeout (90 seconds) bound what an unattended run can do
weaknesses: python_execute runs arbitrary Python inside the editor process and the only confirmation mechanism found is the clarify question, so there is no approval step before a script changes the project

Scene summaries, screenshots, attached assets and microphone audio are sent to a remote model endpoint, the built-in file and web search tools are OpenAI-only, and the plugin can read a local Codex auth.json for credentials
Windows-only, marked experimental in the plugin descriptor, with no releases published; the computer-use tool is stubbed out and disabled
why_it_matters: A concrete example of an in-editor agent for a game engine, showing how a domain-specific tool layer plus self-verification can replace a generic code-execution tool.
